reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text twice against saved copies of the Kannada Wikipedia article ಗೋವಿನ ಹಾಡು (song transcription and summary) and the Mysore University Vishwakosha entry.

Ending changed (the song's tiger leaps into the sky and dies; here it leaves) and disclosed in changes, note and contentNote; the precedent is stated accurately (the dove story's rewarded self-immolations).
Caste/community label ಗೊಲ್ಲ replaced by ದನಗಾಹಿ and disclosed; song lines restored to the transcribed wording (ಸಕಲ ಬಳಗ, ಹಾಯದಿರಿ/ಒದೆಯದಿರಿ).

illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536; seams exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024; under 650 KB.
Calf removed from the two hillside panels (the calves stay in the enclosure); a calf-like animal in the distant herd replaced by adult cows; three panels composited from two edit passes.
Punyakoti keeps her white coat, two horns, red-yellow cord and bell; the tiger never touches her; the far tiger in the last panel walks away along a hill, not leaping.
No text, no modern objects, no blood.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher, folklorist or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children or parents.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol in the new stylized 3D look for this collection, and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with seams measured in pixels.
Source fidelity was checked against the Wikipedia transcription and summaries, not a critical edition of the song.
